surprises.head: Seattle couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: Seattle’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 3.0% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.3% and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far less than once in a thousand games. You may never see it again.

story.head: The Kraken beat the Mammoth
paras: Jordan Eberle got the scoring started for the Kraken early in the first, but Vincent Trocheck tied it up for Utah on the power play late in the period. Matty Beniers put the Kraken ahead 2-1 on the power play 26 seconds later. Brandon Montour made it 3-1 on the power play early in the second. The third period was a wild one. Logan Cooley pulled the Mammoth within one on the power play just 27 seconds into the period. Utah had a goal taken off for offside early in the period. Cooley scored again midway through the period to tie it 3-3, but that’s where Utah’s luck ran out. Seattle had a goal taken off for offside later in the period, though it didn’t end up costing them. Mackie Samoskevich put the Kraken ahead for good late in the period, and Frédérick Gaudreau sealed it into the empty net with a minute left.

The Mammoth outshot the Kraken 36-23, but the Kraken’s looks were better, so the chances came out about even. Philipp Grubauer made 33 saves for the Kraken, and Karel Vejmelka stopped 18 of 22. The Kraken improved to 7-3-1, and the Mammoth fell to 7-4-0.

items.text: Nick Schmaltz’s six-game point streak against Seattle ended.
